# TidyWL — YouTube Watch Later Tidy

> Free browser extension for Chrome and Firefox that lets you bulk delete, filter, sort, and actually manage your YouTube Watch Later playlist, your Liked videos, and any playlist you created — and download every video's transcript in one go. Built because YouTube caps Watch Later at 5,000 videos, gives Liked videos no management tools at all, and the official API refuses to touch either.

## What it does

TidyWL gives you a full-screen dashboard for YouTube's Watch Later playlist, inspired by macOS Storage Manager. Since version 1.5.0 the same dashboard also opens your **Liked videos** — a switch in the header moves between them, from either page — with the same breakdowns, search, filters, sorting, export and Gemini Notebook support. Since version 1.6.0 it opens **any playlist you created** as well, from a Playlists menu in the header, and you can **tick several playlists and see them merged**: one card per video, carrying a chip for each playlist it belongs to, so a video saved in three places is one row that tells you all three. From a merged view, moving a video removes it from every ticked playlist it was in. You can also delete a playlist you own outright, confirmed by name; its videos stay on YouTube. Each list keeps its own local cache and its own sync time, so working on one never disturbs the other. You can bulk delete hundreds of videos in seconds, **remove likes in bulk** on the Liked tab through the same flow, see your playlist broken down by channel or by topic, hide topics you are not interested in, search, and filter by title, channel, watched status, availability, or duration — either preset buckets including a Shorts bucket, or your own minimum and maximum in minutes. The watched filter carries an adjustable progress threshold, so you can ask for videos you are at least three-quarters through rather than merely ones you started.

Since version 1.6.0 every video also carries the **tags its uploader gave it** — the keyword field YouTube stores but never displays, plus any hashtags in the description. Search matches those tags, so a video can be found by what it is about rather than only by what it is called, and clicking a tag filters by it; several tags stack, narrowing to the videos that carry all of them. This is what makes search usable on playlists that are not in English: uploaders commonly tag in both the video's language and English, so there is something to match even when the title has nothing. You can sort by playlist order, duration, view count, published date, channel, or title. You can move or copy selected videos into any other playlist, create a playlist inline, reorder with Move to Top and Move to Bottom or by dragging, open every selected video in background tabs, switch between YouTube accounts, and export to JSON or CSV.

Two features go beyond playlist management. **Bulk transcript download** gives you one timestamped text file per video, named after the video title, after first checking with YouTube which videos have captions at all. **Send to Gemini Notebook** (formerly NotebookLM) pushes your selected videos into a notebook as sources, either a new notebook or one you already have.

## Why it exists

YouTube's Watch Later playlist has a hard 5,000 video cap. Once you hit it, YouTube stops adding new videos and gives you no bulk management tools — you have to delete videos one at a time through a three-dot menu. The official YouTube Data API explicitly excludes Watch Later. TidyWL works around this by using your existing logged-in YouTube session, so no account, API key, or OAuth is needed.

## Browser support

- **Chrome** — published on the Chrome Web Store. Also works on Chromium-based browsers such as Edge and Brave.
- **Firefox 153 or newer** — signed by Mozilla but submitted as unlisted, so it is distributed from https://tidywl.com/firefox/ rather than published in the addons.mozilla.org directory. There is no public AMO listing page. It updates automatically from tidywl.com.
- **Firefox for Android** — not supported. YouTube's mobile site is a different page structure and it has not been tested.

Both channels are built from a single source tree and ship the same feature set.

## Ratings

Rated 5.0 out of 5 from 54 reviews on the Chrome Web Store, with over 3,000 users. It also carries Google's "Featured" editorial badge and a verified-publisher checkmark. The rating, review count and user count are published on https://tidywl.com and refreshed weekly from the store listing; the store rounds its user count to a bucket, so 3,000 is a floor rather than an exact figure.

## Usage

TidyWL users have deleted over {{ site.data.usage.deletedTotal }} videos since August 2026 (figure as of {{ site.data.usage.lastUpdated }}, refreshed daily). The running total is shown on https://tidywl.com and published as JSON at https://tidywl.com/api/stats, alongside counts of likes removed and videos moved between playlists. Those totals are the only thing TidyWL reports: each install sends a random identifier that is not linked to any account, plus its own running counts. No video, title, channel, playlist name, timestamp or account ever leaves the browser as part of it. Firefox users can switch reporting off from the add-on's permissions panel; the full description is at https://tidywl.com/privacy/.

## Technical details

TidyWL works by reading the user's active YouTube session (SAPISID cookie and session index from window.ytcfg) and calling YouTube's internal InnerTube API the same way the YouTube web app does. No OAuth, no API key, no stored tokens. The extension only functions while the user is actively logged into YouTube. Because it depends on undocumented internal endpoints, it fetches a small public configuration file from tidywl.com at runtime so that many YouTube-side changes can be patched without shipping a store update.

## Privacy

TidyWL runs in your browser. No account, and your YouTube data — titles, video IDs, channels, playlists — never leaves it. Network calls go to YouTube's own endpoints using your existing session, and to a public config file on tidywl.com that carries no identifiers and no payload. Since version 1.6.0 the extension also sends tidywl.com one small usage report: a random identifier generated on install (not linked to any Google account) plus lifetime counts of videos deleted, likes removed, videos moved, bulk operations run, the size of the Watch Later playlist, and the browser name. It is sent only when a count changes, never carries a title, video ID, channel or timestamp, has no off switch on Chrome (uninstalling stops it), is controlled on Firefox by the Technical and interaction data toggle, and records idle for 12 months are deleted. One feature is an explicit exception you trigger yourself: Send to Gemini Notebook passes the video links you selected to Google's Gemini Notebook using your own Google session. It is opt-in per use and gated behind a browser permission prompt. Full policy: https://tidywl.com/privacy/

## Limitations

- Deletions are permanent; YouTube provides no undo. The same is true of removed likes.
- Removing a like is not a playlist edit — YouTube treats it as un-liking the video, which can change what it recommends.
- Reordering is not available on Liked videos: YouTube orders that list by when you liked something.
- Favorites, and playlists you saved but do not own, can be searched and cleaned up but not reordered — YouTube serves those without the per-item handle reordering needs.
- A merged view of several playlists supports copy and move, but not delete or reorder; narrow to one playlist for those.
- Deleting a playlist is permanent. Its videos stay on YouTube; the playlist does not.
- Bulk deletion is necessarily sequential, because YouTube rejects parallel playlist edits, so large batches take time.
- "Playlist order" is not date-added — YouTube does not expose per-video add timestamps on the web.
- Transcript download opens a small visible window and takes roughly three seconds per video; videos without captions are reported as skipped.
- Free Gemini Notebook accounts cap a notebook at 50 sources.
- The cache is local to each browser and does not sync across devices.
